2.  23-25690  Recommendation to receive and file all subcommittee reports.

  Policies and Standards

  Alexa Dixson-Griggs, the Long Beach CoC Coordinator, provided an update on
  program monitoring. The Homeless Service Bureau is working on a standardized
  plan to create a formal action plan. The plan will help hold subrecipients to a
  consistent standard across the board but also provide grant guidance when
  necessary.

  Coordinated Entry System Policies and Procedures

  Alexa Dixson-Griggs, the Long Beach CoC Coordinator, provided an update.
  Conference calls with subrecipients regarding coordinated entry and matching are
  underway and have been almost a month. The goal is to match clients who are high
  utilizers of system resources once the HOP is cleaned up. With that goal in mind,
  the HSB team is working on an inactivity policy surrounding clients no longer active
  in HMIS/ equivalent databases.

  HMIS Policies and Procedures and Data Quality Plan

  Alexa Dixson-Griggs, the Long Beach CoC Coordinator, provided an update. The
  HSB is working towards moving the coordinated entry to Long Beach HMIS. This
  will allow for streamlined access and referrals to Long Beach’s permanent
  supportive housing resources. She also provided a brief overview of the Data HUD
  standards for 2024 (October 1st); some data points changed: race & ethnicity,
  social security number, and gender.

  A motion was made by Member Brezenoff, seconded by Co-Chair Shuford, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  9 Wee, Shuford, Tan, Topolewski, Brezenoff, Kennedy, Pezzelle,
  Richert, Martins
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 8 Washington, Weithers, Howat, Lee Lawler, Wilson, Chotiswatdi,
  Bambrick, Boyce

3.  23-25691  Recommendation to receive and file the Strategic Plan Update

  Alexa Dixson-Griggs, the Long Beach CoC Coordinator, provided an update on the
  Strategic Plan. The Lived Experience Board has met and is working on finalizing its
  short-term goals within the next meeting. The first meeting was very introductory

4.  23-25692  Recommendation to receive and file Leasing Updates.

  Alexa Dixson-Griggs, the Long Beach CoC Coordinator, updated the group on the
  current status of the Lease ups.
  • Heritage Gardens: 34 total units, 24 matches requested.
  • The Cove: 90 total units, 60 matches requested.
  • HSV’s: 79 total units, 150 matches requested.
  • 26.2: 77 total units, 84 matches requested.
  • Wellspring: 87 total units, 20 matches requested.
  She proudly announced that CES is turning people from the HOP into housing.

  A motion was made by Co-Chair Shuford, seconded by Member Brezenoff, to

5.  23-25693  Recommendation to approve the Continuum of Care Charter Amendment.

  Jeffrey Proctor, Homeless Services Admin & Operations Officer, presented the
  Continuum of Care Charter Amendment.
  • In 2022, the Long Beach CoC and Homeless Services Bureau partnered with
  UCLA Luskin School of Public Affairs to evaluate the need for formally
  establishing a Lived Experience group to advise the CoC on program and
  policy decisions and advance equity within the CoC.
  • The presentation slides and recommendations were presented by HSB and
  UCLA staff to the CoC board on June 14, 2022.
  • The Lived Experience Advisory Board (LEAB) is a leadership body of
  members with previous or current lived experience of homelessness. Set
  structure of members to evaluate systems and make policy
  recommendations.
  • The recommendations were as follows:
  • The LEAB will be under the CoC Board as a subcommittee.
  • Provide a stable, yet amendable, baseline structure via LEAB-created
  charter.
  • Paid staff position as a liaison between the City and Board
  • On June 13, 2023 staff presented final recommendations regarding the
  proposed structure of the Lived Experience Advisory Board. Recommended
  to be established as a CoC subcommittee and presented on the draft LEAB
  interest form. Member recruitment began in late August.
  • Information on the meeting will be posted on Legistar and accessible to the
  public.

  A motion was made by Member Topolewski, seconded by Member Richert, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  10 Wee, Shuford, Tan, Topolewski, Brezenoff, Kennedy, Pezzelle,
  Richert, Martins, Chotiswatdi
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 7 Washington, Weithers, Howat, Lee Lawler, Wilson, Bambrick, Boyce

6.  23-25694  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Services Bureau Operations
  Report.

  City Staff Alexa Dixson-Griggs provided a program update, and Jeffrey Proctor,
  Homeless Services Admin and Operations Officer, provided a funding update.
  • Long Beach Continuum of Care submitted its annual renewal NOFO to HUD
  for $11,371,399 with $1,600,119 in proposals for new projects. The CoC is
  working on this year’s program and billing; there are changes to a few of the
  sub-recipient contracts.

• HMIS has entered into a data agreement sharing with Health Net and is in
  the process of enrolling DMH into Long Beach Clarity. This includes the
  rollout of new data HUD standards, which began on October 1st. Significant
  changes included data regarding race and ethnicity, social security numbers,
  and gender.
• A brief overview of the data shows that the Long Beach System for Q3:
• 2,839 people assisted, program type (3215 unique clients).
• Almost 200 in permanent housing
• 400 in supportive services.
• Funding was received through Senator Gonzalez for $1.25 million for the
  older adult shallow subsidy prevention program.
• HHAP round 5 applications have opened. This is a change regarding the
  HHAP 5 planning, requiring each region to work in partnership with the
  county on what the regional plan will look like for allocations. Long Beach will
  work with LA County, LA City, Glendale, and Pasadena.
• The city identified a new proposed site for the Long Beach Tiny Home
  Community, southeast corner of East Spring St. and California Ave.
  Community engagement has begun.
• The Winter Shelter opens on 11/14/23, the first time in 10 years we open this
  early in November. Staff engaged with LAHSA and First to Service Ministries
  Inc. to add additional bed capacity at 702 W Anaheim for the winter shelter
  program; 40 additional beds are available.
• Enhanced focus on safety in Downtown, including increased collaboration
  and planning, additional MAC Locations in downtown, increased
  programming and activation in Lincoln Park and Billie Jean King Library,
  increased police presence to focus on reducing crime, increased cleaning
  services, and maintenance of public spaces. The press conference
  happened later that day.
• Presentations from Eugene, OR, and Denver, CO, were heard at the
  Homeless Services Advisory Committee regarding the safe sleep program;
  the HSB is working on a report back to the Council on this being a potential
  model for interim housing options and a report will follow in the upcoming
  months.
• Additional staffing has been added to support the MSC call line, Mobile
  therapy van, and substance use services to field-based staff.
• Working on a plan to start the clinician-in-jail program again; this is a
  partnership between HSB and PD.
• Refreshed data on the Data Dashboard occurred on November 3rd.
• Mailers went out in October utility statement soliciting donations for the
  Mayor’s Fund as part of the annual campaign strategy.
• 200 people signed up to volunteer for the 2024 Annual Homeless Count.
• Began engaging motel owners to seek interest in participating in the
  Encampment Resolution program.
• Additional Rapid Rehousing provider was onboarded (April Parker

7.  23-25695  Recommendation to receive and file the CoC Governance Report.

  Co-Chair Kimberly Wee provided an update on CoC Governance. The general
  meeting had minimal participation since it was in person. We can have these in
  person occasionally, but we get more participation via Zoom for the general
  meetings. Leadership will look to post and inform the public as soon as possible
  when the next in-person meeting will be held.

  Co-Chair Kimberly Wee requested to add a presentation on increased mental
  health services that are available and what is the process and expectations for
  mental health services.

PUBLIC COMMENT

  • There are volunteer opportunities for Christmas toy wrapping on Thursday, 12/14/23. It is a
  great event to help give back to the community. Parents can take their children to get a
  Christmas toy.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

  • Co-Chair Kimberly Wee provided updates regarding open positions at the Cabrillo Village,
  encouraged anyone who wishes to apply, and passed the message around to anyone
  interested. Openings are posted on Indeed.

ADJOURNMENT

Co-Chair Kimberly Wee adjourned the meeting at 4:13 PM.
